summary: Robert Hinde studied at St John's College (~1941–1947) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1947–1950). He held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1950–1994), where he taught John Hurrell Crook.

Active in Indology and linguistics, Robert Hunter studied at Marischal College, Aberdeen (~1836–1841), the University of Aberdeen (~1836–1841), and the University of Edinburgh (~1841–1845). He served as a missionary at the Free Church of Scotland Mission (1846–1855).

Historian and Indologist Robert I. Crane earned his B.A. at Duke (~1937–1941) and Ph.D. at Yale (~1948–1951). He taught at the University of Chicago, University of Michigan, and Duke, later serving as Ford-Maxwell Professor at Syracuse University (1968–1990).

Robert Isaac Levy worked in Indology and religious studies. He was Professor of Anthropology at the University of California, San Diego (1969–1991), a Research Professor at UNC Chapel Hill (~1991–2003), and held a post at Duke University.

Working in Tibetology and religious studies, Robert J. Miller earned degrees from Michigan and Washington (Ph.D. ~1949–1958). He held posts at the University of Washington, the American Institute of Indian Studies, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (Professor, 1959–1988).
Robert J. Topmiller, a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at the University of Kentucky under the doctoral supervision of George C. Herring.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Robert Kritzer completed his PhD at UC Berkeley in 1995 under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held posts at UC Berkeley and served as Associate Professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).
Robert Kyd studied at the University of Edinburgh and founded the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden in 1787.

Robert L. Brown worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was Professor Emeritus of Art History at UCLA (~1983–2014) and served as a curator in South and Southeast Asian art at LACMA (~1999–2014).

Indologist and linguist Robert Lenz studied at Tartu and under Franz Bopp in Berlin (Dr. Ph. 1831–1832). He held posts at the Tallinn Cathedral School, Breslau, the Russian Academy of Sciences, and was Professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg (1835–1836).

Indologist and historian Robert Lingat studied at the University of Paris (Dr., 1931). He taught law at Thammasat, the University of Indochina, Saigon, and EPHE, also teaching at the University of Cambodia and INALCO.

Robert M. Gimello was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who earned his PhD from Columbia in 1976. He served as department head and professor emeritus at the University of Arizona (~1981–2001) and professor at Harvard (~2001–2007).

Active in Indology and history, Robert Maclagan studied at the University of Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and the Royal School of Military Engineering. He served as Principal of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

Philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar Robert Magliola completed his Ph.D. at Princeton (~1966–1970). He held faculty posts at Purdue, Tamkang, National Taiwan University, Assumption University of Thailand (~1993–2003), and was a seminar associate at Columbia (2002–2011).

Robert Mason Towers, an Indologist and linguist, earned an M.A. from Trinity College Dublin. He served as Professor of Bengali at King's College London (1888) and as a University Teacher at the University of Cambridge (1897–1907).

Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar Robert Mayer earned his Ph.D. at Leiden, supervised by Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen. He held posts at the Universities of Kent, Wales, and Oxford (Oriental Studies faculty, 2002).

Robert Needham Cust, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at Eton, Trinity College Cambridge, East India Company College, Fort William College, and Edinburgh (LL.D. 1885). He served in the Bengal Civil Service from ~1843 to 1867.
Robert Orme, an Indologist and historian, studied at Harrow School until 1741 and served as Historiographer for the East India Company from 1769 to 1801.

Indologist Robert P. Goldman studied at Columbia and Penn (Ph.D. ~1965–1971) under Ludo Rocher, S. D. Joshi, and T. S. Shastri. In ~1971, he became the Magistretti Distinguished Professor at UC Berkeley.

Robert P. Scharlemann, a religious studies and philosophy scholar, studied at Concordia College, Concordia Seminary, and Heidelberg University. He held faculty posts at the University of Southern California (~1963–1966), University of Iowa (~1966–1981), and University of Virginia (~1981–2001).
